Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls, sounding very upset, and asks if you have a moment to talk about a recent argument with their partner.
Expectation2: Assemble and construct wooden frameworks, furniture, or cabinetry
Situation2: The carpenter is building custom cabinetry and needs to collaborate with other construction professionals to complete the project on time
Story: I was in the middle of measuring out the panels for a custom cabinet job, sawdust clinging to my shirt, when my phone buzzed. It was Jamie, my oldest friend. Her voice trembled as she asked if I had a moment—she’d just had a huge fight with her partner and needed someone to talk to. I glanced at the half-assembled frame in front of me, the blueprints spread out, and the clock ticking down to the deadline. The electrician was waiting for my part to be finished so he could start wiring, and the contractor had already called twice to check on my progress. But Jamie’s voice was raw, and I knew she wouldn’t have reached out unless she really needed me. My mind raced, torn between the expectation to be there for my friend and the responsibility to keep the project on track. I could hear the hum of the construction site around me, but all I could focus on was the weight of both roles pressing in, demanding more than I felt able to give.
